feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament
entry.summary: Russians head to the polls to choose lawmakers for their parliament, the Duma. It's Russia's first nationwide parliamentary race since launching its full scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

entry.title: When Trump and Xi meet they will discuss AI. 'Track Two' talks are already buzzing
entry.summary: An informal network of dialogues at think tanks and universities is bringing together experts from the U.S. and China to talk about the shared perils of AI — and possible paths forward.

entry.title: Syrian regime planned American journalist's kidnapping for weeks
entry.summary: New reporting finds the abduction of journalist Austin Tice was planned by the Syrian government for weeks.

entry.title: Will even one of the U.N.'s 17 'sustainable development goals' be met by 2030?
entry.summary: The 17 goals agreed upon by world leaders are incredibly ambitious. Are we even close to achieving any of them? If we don't, is the project a failure?

entry.title: Judge says Trump can't demolish Kennedy Center. And, lawsuits target voter intimidation
entry.summary: A federal judge ruled yesterday that President Trump cannot tear down the Kennedy Center without a 30-day notice. And, recent lawsuits seek to keep armed federal officers away from polling sites.

entry.title: Ms. Rachel has entered her album era, and she is so happy about it
entry.summary: Ms. Rachel has conquered YouTube, Netflix and the toy aisle. Now she's making an album, with real instruments, big feelings and her littlest listeners in mind.

entry.title: South Africa 'feels like a prison' for women amid spate of femicides
entry.summary: South Africa has some of the highest rates of violence against women in the world, and a spate of killings of nine women in the same area in recent weeks has led to renewed outrage.

entry.title: Poland's prime minister warns of Russian 'accidental' attacks on Ukraine's allies
entry.summary: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said that these potential strikes "intend to paralyze NATO" in an attempt to demonstrate that Article 5 "exists only in theory."

entry.title: What to know after a week of Houthi attacks that threaten Saudi oil
entry.summary: The Houthis' biggest land grab in years reignited Yemen's 12-year civil war and pushed up global fuel prices, extending their reach to a key maritime chokepoint and threatening Saudi Arabia's oil exports.

entry.title: Behind the overture from the European Union to Canada
entry.summary: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with Ian Bremmer, president and founder of the Eurasia Group, about the latest developments between Canada, the European Union and the U.S.
